# Passes 3670–3686 — Monster, tomotope, universal amalgamation, and the third 192

passes every exact source check and reproduces the semantic certificate

`2d5fe418bb2bbee0eb479e42d22dd47d31c37f7d5f8be6b1732acf0dc1db8b78`.

# I. Prior-art reconciliation: chambers are spreads

Passes 3663–3669 proved an objectwise, generator-equivariant bijection

\[
\{36\ A_6\text{ chambers}\}
\longleftrightarrow
\{36\ W(3,3)\text{ spreads}\}.
\]

For distinct chambers \(H,K\), the complete intersection dictionary is

\[
|H\cap K|=12\iff |\Sigma_H\cap\Sigma_K|=4,
\]

and

\[
|H\cap K|=18\iff |\Sigma_H\cap\Sigma_K|=1.
\]

Consequently the order-12 relation is

\[
\operatorname{SRG}(36,15,6,6),
\qquad
15^1\oplus3^{15}\oplus(-3)^{20},
\]

while its complement is

\[
\operatorname{SRG}(36,20,10,12),
\qquad
20^1\oplus2^{20}\oplus(-4)^{15}.
\]

The present verifier independently reconstructs these two relations and the U4(2) suborbit lengths

\[
1+15+20,
\]

but does not reclaim them as new. They provide the exact carrier on which the new clique and tomotope computations run.

# II. The 135 maximal K4s

The valency-15 chamber graph contains exactly

\[
\boxed{135}
\]

maximal four-cliques. U4(2) acts transitively on them. Every one of the 36 chambers lies in exactly 15 such cliques, so the total chamber–clique incidence count is

\[
36\cdot15=135\cdot4=\boxed{540}.
\]

This is the first structural explanation in this packet for the repeated 540 carrier count. It is not being identified with every other occurrence of 540 in the repository; it is specifically the flag-like incidence set

\[
\{(\Sigma,C):\Sigma\in C,\ C\cong K_4\}.
\]

The stabilizer of one maximal K4 has order

\[
25,920/135=\boxed{192}.
\]

Its exact element-order census is

\[
1^1\,2^{43}\,3^{32}\,4^{84}\,6^{32}.
\]

Its center has order two.

# III. The third 192: a non-split tomotope lift

The tomotope literature gives a faithful edge action of its automorphism group on twelve edges, generated by

\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_0&=(5\,10)(6\,9)(7\,12)(8\,11),\\
\rho_1&=(1\,6)(2\,5)(3\,8)(4\,7),\\
\rho_2&=(5\,9)(6\,10)(7\,11)(8\,12),\\
\rho_3&=(5\,8)(6\,7)(9\,12)(10\,11).
\end{aligned}
\]

The generated group has order 96 and order census

\[
1^1\,2^{27}\,3^{32}\,4^{36}.
\]

The new computation quotients the order-192 K4 stabilizer by its center and then searches for four quotient involutions with the exact marked pair orders

\[
|\rho_0\rho_1|=3,
\quad |\rho_0\rho_2|=|\rho_0\rho_3|=2,
\quad |\rho_1\rho_2|=3,
\quad |\rho_1\rho_3|=4,
\quad |\rho_2\rho_3|=2.
\]

A breadth-first word transport proves a bijective marked homomorphism, not merely equality of order profiles. Hence

\[
\boxed{
1\longrightarrow C_2
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Stab}_{U_4(2)}(K_4)
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Aut}(T)
\longrightarrow1.
}
\]

The extension is non-split. Indeed, the split direct product

\[
C_2\times\operatorname{Aut}(T)
\]

would have order census

\[
1^1\,2^{55}\,3^{32}\,4^{72}\,6^{32},
\]

which differs from the observed stabilizer census.

The repository previously distinguished two mechanisms carrying the number 192:

1. 192 as the automorphism order of an intermediate semiregular precursor;
2. 192 as the tomotope flag count \(2\cdot96\).

The chamber calculation supplies a third mechanism:

3. 192 as a non-split central lift of the marked tomotope automorphism group.

This is not numerology. The quotient map and marked generator isomorphism are explicit and executable.

# IV. The four-parabolic amalgam is thick, not polytopal

Let \(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3\) be the four order-three transvections from Passes 3635–3648, and define the four three-generator subgroups

\[
P_i=\langle g_j:j\neq i\rangle.
\]

Each \(P_i\) has order 648 and fixes exactly one W33 point. The full intersection data is

\[
\{|P_i\cap P_j|:i<j\}=\{24,24,24,24,24,54\},
\]

\[
|P_i\cap P_j\cap P_k|=3
\qquad\text{for every triple},
\]

and

\[
P_0\cap P_1\cap P_2\cap P_3=1.
\]

The corresponding coset geometry has forty objects of each of four types and

\[
25,920
\]

chambers. However, deleting any one type leaves a rank-one residue of size

\[
\frac{|P_i\cap P_j\cap P_k|}{|P_0\cap P_1\cap P_2\cap P_3|}=3.
\]

Thus every panel lies in three chambers.

An abstract polytope satisfies the diamond condition: a rank-one interval contains exactly two elements, and its exchange map is an involution. Here the natural panel motion is instead

\[
C_3.
\]

Therefore the exact verdict is

\[
\boxed{
\text{the four-parabolic coset geometry is a thick chamber system, not an abstract polytope.}
}
\]

This locates the amalgamation failure more precisely than the earlier divisibility and string-C-group obstructions. The local parabolics exist; the total core is trivial; the full group is generated; but the final diamond axiom fails by one chamber per panel.

## Relation to the 11-cell, 57-cell, and universal amalgamation

The repository already proves that the common local amalgam

\[
A_5*_{D_{10}}A_5
\]

has three finite completions in the relevant family:

\[
A_6\cong PSL(2,9),\qquad PSL(2,11),\qquad PSL(2,19).
\]

The first is the internal U4(2) chamber core; the latter two govern the 11-cell and 57-cell. Hartley's classification gives seventeen universal rank-four locally projective polytopes and 441 quotients. The new panel computation explains why the four-parabolic U4(2) construction does not provide an additional regular member: it is not thin.

A possible regular cover would have to binary-resolve each ternary panel, perhaps by a sheet, voltage, or Cayley extension. That is now a precise construction problem rather than an unspecified failure of the intersection property.

# V. Non-scalar discriminant cancellation closes at II(24,24)

The previous packet proved that scalar rescaling cannot turn the rank-24 projector lattice into a unimodular positive-definite lattice. Let \(G\) be any nonsingular integral Gram matrix for the rank-24 carrier. Form

\[
\mathcal G=
\begin{pmatrix}
G&I\\
I&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Elementary block determinant identities give

\[
\det\mathcal G=1.
\]

Because \(G\) is even and the lower diagonal block is zero, \(\mathcal G\) is even. For the positive-definite W33 Gram matrix, its inertia is

\[
(24,24).
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{\mathcal G\cong II_{24,24}.}
\]

This is the first exact non-scalar glue closure of the projector lattice: every local discriminant obstruction cancels. It also gives a sharp no-go for the immediate Leech interpretation. The canonical cancellation is necessarily indefinite; it does not produce a positive-definite rank-24 lattice or Leech embedding.

The surviving route must impose a positive polarization, choose a maximal positive subspace compatible with an integral structure, or couple a different auxiliary discriminant form rather than the hyperbolic dual.

# VI. The complete equivariant commutative product envelope

Let \(V\) be the 24-dimensional W33 projector module. The exact character census over all 25,920 group elements is

\[
\chi_V(g)\in\{-1,0,2,3,6,8,24\},
\]

with multiplicities

\[
6624,16530,2160,480,80,45,1.
\]

Character inner products give

\[
\boxed{\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{U_4(2)}(\operatorname{Sym}^2V,V)=2}
\]

and

\[
\boxed{\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{U_4(2)}(\Lambda^2V,V)=1}.
\]

Two explicit commutative products are constructed:

1. project coordinatewise multiplication in the forty-coordinate model back to \(V\);
2. for each W33 point, sum the cross-products over the twelve adjacent triangles through that point, then project back to \(V\).

They are linearly independent and therefore span the entire two-dimensional equivariant commutative product space. Lowering an output index with the invariant Gram form makes each structure tensor fully symmetric, so both products satisfy the Frobenius invariance condition.

## Associativity no-go

Write the general equivariant commutative product as

\[
x\star y=\alpha\,m_0(x,y)+\beta\,m_1(x,y).
\]

Every associator coordinate is a homogeneous quadratic polynomial in \((\alpha,\beta)\). After setting \(t=\alpha/\beta\), 542 nonzero associator polynomials are obtained over

\[
\mathbf F_{1,000,003}.
\]

Their greatest common divisor is one. A small coprime witness pair is

\[
-25t^2-100t-100,
\qquad
-9t^2-292t+76.
\]

Neither endpoint product is associative either. Hence no projective parameter \([\alpha:\beta]\) works modulo this prime, and therefore no nonzero rational product can be associative:

\[
\boxed{
\text{the full U4(2)-equivariant commutative Frobenius envelope contains no nonzero associative algebra.}
}
\]

This does not rule out a Griess-type algebra, because Griess and axial algebras are generally nonassociative. It does show that any claimed multiplication is forced into this two-dimensional envelope and must satisfy additional Monster fusion, idempotent, positivity, and class constraints there.

# VII. Six class-dependent McKay–Thompson channels

The prime support of

\[
|U_4(2)|=2^6\,3^4\,5
\]

selects the three prime pairs

\[
2A/2B,\qquad3A/3B,\qquad5A/5B.
\]

For \(p\in\{2,3,5\}\), let

\[
r=\frac{24}{p-1}.
\]

The exact eta channels are

\[
T_{pB}(\tau)
=
\left(\frac{\eta(\tau)}{\eta(p\tau)}\right)^r+r,
\]

and

\[
T_{pA}(\tau)
=
T_{pB}(\tau)
+p^{r/2}
\left(\frac{\eta(p\tau)}{\eta(\tau)}\right)^r.
\]

The first coefficients after \(q^{-1}\) are:

| class | \(q\) | \(q^2\) | \(q^3\) | \(q^4\) | \(q^5\) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2A | 4372 | 96256 | 1240002 | 10698752 | 74428120 |
| 2B | 276 | -2048 | 11202 | -49152 | 184024 |
| 3A | 783 | 8672 | 65367 | 371520 | 1741655 |
| 3B | 54 | -76 | -243 | 1188 | -1384 |
| 5A | 134 | 760 | 3345 | 12256 | 39350 |
| 5B | 9 | 10 | -30 | 6 | -25 |

This advances the previous scalar \(J+24\) completion to six class-dependent graded channels. It does not construct a Monster module or prove that the W33 carrier realizes these traces. It supplies the exact target series that a future U4(2)-inside-Monster restriction must meet.

# VIII. Bonkers spectral firewall: two fifteens are not one

The W33 point graph has a 15-dimensional eigenspace at eigenvalue \(-4\). The complement of the 36-chamber graph also has a 15-dimensional eigenspace at eigenvalue \(-4\).

The matching pair

\[
(15,-4)
\]

is highly suggestive, but it is insufficient. The verifier transports the U4(2) action to both spaces and computes their characters over the entire group.

Each character has norm one:

\[
\langle\chi_W,\chi_W\rangle
=
\langle\chi_C,\chi_C\rangle=1,
\]

so both modules are irreducible. Their cross inner product is

\[
\boxed{\langle\chi_W,\chi_C\rangle=0.}
\]

Therefore they are inequivalent irreducible U4(2) modules. There is no nonzero equivariant intertwiner between them.

This is an exact spectral-doppelgänger firewall:

\[
\boxed{
\text{equal dimension and equal graph eigenvalue do not imply equal group module.}
}
\]

Any future bridge between the two fifteens must twist by an outer automorphism, enlarge the group, use a nonlinear functor, or break equivariance.

# IX. Monster embedding front: the correct fail-closed target

The complete internal A5 census found 1,296 pairs of A5 subgroups intersecting in D10. Every one of these pairs generates A6, not the full U4(2). Thus a bare instruction to search the Monster for “two D10-sharing A5s that generate U4(2)” omits essential chamber or ambient information.

The repository now exposes a stricter four-generator target:

- four Monster elements of order three;
- pair-product orders \(3,6,6,6,6,6\);
- every three-generator closure has order 648;
- the full closure has order 25,920;
- an independent class-fusion certificate verifies the documented 5B-containing embedding type.

The harness

`analysis/w33_pass3670_3686_mmgroup_four_parabolic_harness.py`

accepts version-stable `mmgroup` strings or integers and independently recomputes the closure orders. The candidate file remains

`status: PENDING`.

Therefore no Monster-word embedding is claimed in this packet.
